title: P300 dataset BI2015b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 44 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface (BCI) videogame called Brain Invaders. The experiment employed an oddball paradigm with a 6×6 grid of 36 symbols (1 target, 35 non-targets) flashed pseudo-randomly across three sessions with varying flash durations (110ms, 80ms, 50ms). EEG signals were acquired using 32 active wet electrodes at 512 Hz, with real-time adaptive classification to assess participant commands in a calibration-free BCI paradigm.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 44 subjects using 32 active wet Silver/Silver Chloride electrodes (10-10 montage) at 512 Hz sampling rate with a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec). The experiment consisted of three game sessions of 9 levels each with different flash durations (110ms, 80ms, 50ms), with resting state and eyes-closed recordings before and after. Each repetition consisted of 12 pseudo-random flashes of six-symbol groups. A real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean (RMDM) classifier was used for online feedback in a calibration-free paradigm. USB digital-to-analog converter synchronization was employed to reduce timing jitter.
